Decision [rust-lang-rust-revert-149375]
Context: Perform many const checks in typeck
Chosen: Perform many const checks in typeck
Rejected/Reverted: reverted in #154930: Revert performing basic const checks in typeck on stable
Why it was not used: It was reverted because it unintentionally produced compilation errors for constants in unreachable code, which requires a formal approval process first.
Evidence: PR #149375 / revert PR #154930

Decision [rust-lang-rust-revert-148937]
Context: Remove initialized-bytes tracking from `BorrowedBuf` and `BorrowedCursor`
Chosen: Remove initialized-bytes tracking from `BorrowedBuf` and `BorrowedCursor`
Rejected/Reverted: reverted in #150096: Revert #148937
Why it was not used: The change was reverted because it degraded performance by forcing reused memory buffers to undergo redundant re-initialization across repeated read operations.
Evidence: PR #148937 / revert PR #150096

Decision [rust-lang-rust-revert-149060]
Context: early return on duplicate span lowerings
Chosen: early return on duplicate span lowerings
Rejected/Reverted: reverted in #149757: Revert "early return on duplicate span lowerings"
Why it was not used: The change was rolled back because it introduced unexpectedly severe compiler performance slowdowns.
Evidence: PR #149060 / revert PR #149757

Decision [rust-lang-rust-revert-149516]
Context: Stop adding MSYS2 to PATH
Chosen: Stop adding MSYS2 to PATH
Rejected/Reverted: reverted in #149600: Revert #149516 to fix i686-pc-windows-gnu host
Why it was not used: The change was reverted because it led distribution builds to include an incompatible 64-bit threading library, breaking the 32-bit Windows toolchain.
Evidence: PR #149516 / revert PR #149600

Decision [rust-lang-rust-revert-142034]
Context: Detect method not being present that is present in other tuple types
Chosen: Detect method not being present that is present in other tuple types
Rejected/Reverted: reverted in #145765: Revert suggestions for missing methods in tuples
Why it was not used: The feature was backed out because it triggered compiler crashes during diagnostic output that affected stable builds, necessitating a rollback while a permanent resolution is developed.
Evidence: PR #142034 / revert PR #145765

Decision [kubernetes-kubernetes-revert-140448]
Context: client-go: prevent unbounded goroutine growth in EventBroadcaster
Chosen: client-go: prevent unbounded goroutine growth in EventBroadcaster
Rejected/Reverted: reverted in #140990: Revert "client-go: prevent unbounded goroutine growth in EventBroadcaster"
Why it was not used: The commit was rolled back because the subsequent patch carried too much risk right before the release candidate milestone.
Evidence: PR #140448 / revert PR #140990

Decision [kubernetes-kubernetes-revert-306]
Context: Solved data races in pkg/registry
Chosen: Solved data races in pkg/registry
Rejected/Reverted: reverted in #140294: Bump SMD to v6.4.2 to revert #306 to fix regression in SSA for nullable container types
Why it was not used: The change was rolled back because it introduced a server-side apply bug that caused valid list and map updates to fail with unexpected 422 validation errors.
Evidence: PR #306 / revert PR #140294

Decision [kubernetes-kubernetes-revert-136254]
Context: Extend PostFilterResult with a list of victim Pods
Chosen: Extend PostFilterResult with a list of victim Pods
Rejected/Reverted: reverted in #137662: Revert "Extend PostFilterResult with a list of victim Pods"
Why it was not used: The update was reverted because delayed preemption was removed from the 1.36 roadmap, making the additional architectural complexity pointless.
Evidence: PR #136254 / revert PR #137662

Decision [kubernetes-kubernetes-revert-126794]
Context: Add e2e test for Regular Container image change
Chosen: Add e2e test for Regular Container image change
Rejected/Reverted: reverted in #130965: Revert "Add e2e test for Regular Container image change"
Why it was not used: The change was rolled back because it caused failures in the main branch's release-blocking test suite.
Evidence: PR #126794 / revert PR #130965

Decision [kubernetes-kubernetes-revert-127300]
Context: [FG:InPlacePodVerticalScaling] kubelet: Propagate error in doPodResizeAction() to the caller
Chosen: [FG:InPlacePodVerticalScaling] kubelet: Propagate error in doPodResizeAction() to the caller
Rejected/Reverted: reverted in #128694: Revert "[FG:InPlacePodVerticalScaling] kubelet: Propagate error in doPodResizeAction() to the caller"
Why it was not used: The commit was reverted because it caused cgroup configuration to constantly trigger errors, which broke the vast majority of pod resizing attempts.
Evidence: PR #127300 / revert PR #128694

Decision [elastic-elasticsearch-revert-154503]
Context: Consolidate fallback storage routing logic into central location
Chosen: Consolidate fallback storage routing logic into central location
Rejected/Reverted: reverted in #156367: Revert "Consolidate fallback storage routing logic into central location" and unmute tests
Why it was not used: The change was reverted because it caused multiple test suite failures that required muting.
Evidence: PR #154503 / revert PR #156367

Decision [elastic-elasticsearch-revert-152050]
Context: Remove global ordinals from composite keyword path
Chosen: Remove global ordinals from composite keyword path
Rejected/Reverted: reverted in #152553: Revert composite keyword segment-ordinals path
Why it was not used: The change was rolled back because it introduced an unintended system regression.
Evidence: PR #152050 / revert PR #152553

Decision [elastic-elasticsearch-revert-151875]
Context: Use a bulk scorer for rescoring vectors
Chosen: Use a bulk scorer for rescoring vectors
Rejected/Reverted: reverted in #152097: Revert "Use a bulk scorer for rescoring vectors"
Why it was not used: It was reverted because certain test seeds triggered failures by attempting to read from an already depleted iterator, with the underlying cause being unclear.
Evidence: PR #151875 / revert PR #152097

Decision [elastic-elasticsearch-revert-120214]
Context: [TEST] Use Docker Compose v2 for TestFixturePlugin
Chosen: [TEST] Use Docker Compose v2 for TestFixturePlugin
Rejected/Reverted: reverted in #120294: Revert "[TEST] Use Docker Compose v2 for TestFixturePlugin"
Why it was not used: The change triggered test failures on AmazonLinux 2023, and the Docker version conflict was resolved directly inside the virtual machine images instead.
Evidence: PR #120214 / revert PR #120294

Decision [elastic-elasticsearch-revert-147071]
Context: Enforce single values for text fields and ip fields when multi_value=no is configured in the mapping (multi_value=no part 3/5)
Chosen: Enforce single values for text fields and ip fields when multi_value=no is configured in the mapping (multi_value=no part 3/5)
Rejected/Reverted: reverted in #147360: Revert "Enforce single values when multi_value=no is configured on fields with doc values (#147071)"
Why it was not used: It was reverted because faulty feature gating caused new tests to fail on mixed-version clusters and break the CI pipeline.
Evidence: PR #147071 / revert PR #147360

Decision [kep-keps-sig-storage-1979-object-storage-support]
Context: KEP-1979: Object Storage Support
Chosen: KEP-1979: Object Storage Support
Alternative considered: Automatically mount buckets to Pods
Why it was not used: Diverse application requirements and access methods made it infeasible to build a standardized mounting approach that works for every workload and driver.
Evidence: keps/sig-storage/1979-object-storage-support/README.md

Decision [kep-keps-sig-storage-1979-object-storage-support]
Context: KEP-1979: Object Storage Support
Chosen: KEP-1979: Object Storage Support
Alternative considered: Encode BucketAccess connection information in a JSON blob
Why it was not used: Driver authors struggled to parse a single JSON payload, preferring distinct Secret entries that can be mounted flexibly via env vars or separate files.
Evidence: keps/sig-storage/1979-object-storage-support/README.md

Decision [kep-keps-sig-storage-1979-object-storage-support]
Context: KEP-1979: Object Storage Support
Chosen: KEP-1979: Object Storage Support
Alternative considered: Cross-resource protection finalizers
Why it was not used: The team avoided them because manual deletion by users causes system errors, opting instead to manage cross-resource dependencies with annotations.
Evidence: keps/sig-storage/1979-object-storage-support/README.md

Decision [kep-keps-sig-storage-1979-object-storage-support]
Context: KEP-1979: Object Storage Support
Chosen: KEP-1979: Object Storage Support
Alternative considered: Bucket creation annotation
Why it was not used: Developers deemed this safeguard unnecessary for COSI during design planning, though it may be added later as an internal detail if required.
Evidence: keps/sig-storage/1979-object-storage-support/README.md

Decision [kep-keps-sig-storage-1979-object-storage-support]
Context: KEP-1979: Object Storage Support
Chosen: KEP-1979: Object Storage Support
Alternative considered: BucketClass field on Bucket resource
Why it was not used: The project chose to manage binding exclusively via bucket claim references, removing the need to record the class on the bucket resource.
Evidence: keps/sig-storage/1979-object-storage-support/README.md

Decision [kep-keps-sig-storage-1979-object-storage-support]
Context: KEP-1979: Object Storage Support
Chosen: KEP-1979: Object Storage Support
Alternative considered: Updating BucketAccess Secrets
Why it was not used: Never overwriting existing secrets prevented administrators from rotating credentials and blocked systems from updating connection endpoints or locations.
Evidence: keps/sig-storage/1979-object-storage-support/README.md

Decision [kep-keps-sig-storage-1979-object-storage-support]
Context: KEP-1979: Object Storage Support
Chosen: KEP-1979: Object Storage Support
Alternative considered: BucketAccess static provisioning
Why it was not used: It was rejected because implementing it would be overly complex, prone to defects, and unable to enforce consistent behavior across different stakeholders.
Evidence: keps/sig-storage/1979-object-storage-support/README.md

Decision [kep-keps-sig-storage-1979-object-storage-support]
Context: KEP-1979: Object Storage Support
Chosen: KEP-1979: Object Storage Support
Alternative considered: BucketAccess Read/Write AccessMode
Why it was not used: Storage backends define data and metadata rights inconsistently, making a unified access mode difficult to implement without compromising administrator control.
Evidence: keps/sig-storage/1979-object-storage-support/README.md

Decision [kep-keps-sig-storage-1979-object-storage-support]
Context: KEP-1979: Object Storage Support
Chosen: KEP-1979: Object Storage Support
Alternative considered: Handling systems that cannot support multi-bucket BucketAccesses
Why it was not used: Dropping multi-bucket access ignores strong user demand, while tracking driver capability combinations harms portability and introduces excessive design complexity.
Evidence: keps/sig-storage/1979-object-storage-support/README.md

Decision [kep-keps-sig-auth-2718-20210511-client-exec-proxy]
Context: KEP-2718: Client Executable Proxy
Chosen: KEP-2718: Client Executable Proxy
Alternative considered: Alternative Proposal: Request Replacement
Why it was not used: Specifying a dedicated message protocol was deemed too cumbersome and less adaptable to general proxy requirements.
Evidence: keps/sig-auth/2718-20210511-client-exec-proxy/README.md

Decision [kep-keps-sig-cloud-provider-2133-out-of-tree-credential-provider]
Context: Out-of-Tree Credential Providers
Chosen: Out-of-Tree Credential Providers
Alternative considered: API Server Proxy
Why it was not used: It was rejected because it fell outside the proposal's scope, lacked sufficient user demand, and would delay the timeline for removing in-tree cloud providers.
Evidence: keps/sig-cloud-provider/2133-out-of-tree-credential-provider/README.md

Decision [kep-keps-sig-cloud-provider-2133-out-of-tree-credential-provider]
Context: Out-of-Tree Credential Providers
Chosen: Out-of-Tree Credential Providers
Alternative considered: Sidecar Credential Daemon
Why it was not used: This option was rejected because operating a persistent daemon introduces greater complexity than directly invoking a standalone binary.
Evidence: keps/sig-cloud-provider/2133-out-of-tree-credential-provider/README.md

Decision [kep-keps-sig-cloud-provider-2133-out-of-tree-credential-provider]
Context: Out-of-Tree Credential Providers
Chosen: Out-of-Tree Credential Providers
Alternative considered: Bound Service Account Token Flow
Why it was not used: This approach was deferred as outside the immediate scope of extracting cloud-dependent logic, though it remains a possible future enhancement.
Evidence: keps/sig-cloud-provider/2133-out-of-tree-credential-provider/README.md

Decision [kep-keps-sig-cloud-provider-2133-out-of-tree-credential-provider]
Context: Out-of-Tree Credential Providers
Chosen: Out-of-Tree Credential Providers
Alternative considered: Pushing Credential Management into the CRI
Why it was not used: This option was deferred for later evaluation because the extensive architectural overhaul it demanded went beyond the immediate project scope.
Evidence: keps/sig-cloud-provider/2133-out-of-tree-credential-provider/README.md

Decision [rust-lang-rust-revert-144407]
Context: fix(debuginfo): disable overflow check for recursive non-enum types
Chosen: fix(debuginfo): disable overflow check for recursive non-enum types
Rejected/Reverted: reverted in #145979: Revert "fix(debuginfo): disable overflow check for recursive non-enum types"
Why it was not used: The compiler team decided during triage to roll back the PR rather than try to resolve its issues with a forward patch.
Evidence: PR #144407 / revert PR #145979

Decision [kubernetes-kubernetes-revert-129701]
Context: tests: include stdout of failed commands in JUnit
Chosen: tests: include stdout of failed commands in JUnit
Rejected/Reverted: reverted in #129769: Revert "tests: include stdout of failed commands in JUnit"
Why it was not used: The change was reverted because it disrupted TestGrid's result processing, likely due to unsupported characters in the output.
Evidence: PR #129701 / revert PR #129769

Decision [kubernetes-kubernetes-revert-126599]
Context: fix: preserve options after remount for bind mounting
Chosen: fix: preserve options after remount for bind mounting
Rejected/Reverted: reverted in #127899: Revert 126599: fix: preserve options after remount for bind mounting
Why it was not used: The pull request was rolled back because it introduced regressions that caused automated GCE COS test suites to fail.
Evidence: PR #126599 / revert PR #127899

Decision [kep-keps-sig-auth-279-limit-node-access]
Context: Bounding Self-Labeling Kubelets
Chosen: Bounding Self-Labeling Kubelets
Alternative considered: File or flag-based configuration of the apiserver to allow specifying allowed labels
Why it was not used: File configs are difficult to verify and synchronize across replicated control planes, whereas a fixed standard provides consistent cluster behavior and simpler logic.
Evidence: keps/sig-auth/279-limit-node-access/README.md

Decision [kep-keps-sig-auth-279-limit-node-access]
Context: Bounding Self-Labeling Kubelets
Chosen: Bounding Self-Labeling Kubelets
Alternative considered: API-based configuration of the apiserver to allow specifying allowed labels
Why it was not used: Configuring permitted labels via the API could allow compromised nodes to escalate privileges and lacks the consistency of a static rule set.
Evidence: keps/sig-auth/279-limit-node-access/README.md

Decision [kep-keps-sig-auth-279-limit-node-access]
Context: Bounding Self-Labeling Kubelets
Chosen: Bounding Self-Labeling Kubelets
Alternative considered: Allow kubelets to add any labels they wish, and add NoSchedule taints if disallowed labels are added
Why it was not used: This option was rejected because automating taint removal was too complex and tracking which labels caused the taint proved difficult.
Evidence: keps/sig-auth/279-limit-node-access/README.md

Decision [kep-keps-sig-auth-279-limit-node-access]
Context: Bounding Self-Labeling Kubelets
Chosen: Bounding Self-Labeling Kubelets
Alternative considered: Forbid all labels regardless of namespace except for a specifically allowed set
Why it was not used: This was rejected because it disrupted existing node labeling, hindered integration with external systems like CSI, and inappropriately restricted non-Kubernetes label domains.
Evidence: keps/sig-auth/279-limit-node-access/README.md

Decision [kep-keps-sig-cli-2382-kustomize-exec-secret-generator]
Context: Kustomize Exec Secret Generator
Chosen: Kustomize Exec Secret Generator
Alternative considered: Enable Plugins with Environment Variables
Why it was not used: This option was rejected because enabling plugins through environment settings failed to provide meaningful security gains over directory-based controls.
Evidence: keps/sig-cli/2382-kustomize-exec-secret-generator/README.md

Decision [kep-keps-sig-instrumentation-647-apiserver-tracing]
Context: KEP-647: APIServer Tracing
Chosen: KEP-647: APIServer Tracing
Alternative considered: Introducing a new EgressSelector type
Why it was not used: This option was passed over because telemetry does not add a novel traffic target, making existing egress categories sufficient and conventional.
Evidence: keps/sig-instrumentation/647-apiserver-tracing/README.md

Decision [kep-keps-sig-instrumentation-647-apiserver-tracing]
Context: KEP-647: APIServer Tracing
Chosen: KEP-647: APIServer Tracing
Alternative considered: Other OpenTelemetry Exporters
Why it was not used: Vendoring various exporters in-tree was rejected because it would burden the Kubernetes maintainers with selecting and managing an official set of tracing backends.
Evidence: keps/sig-instrumentation/647-apiserver-tracing/README.md

Decision [kep-keps-sig-storage-1790-recover-resize-failure]
Context: Recovery from volume expansion failure
Chosen: Recovery from volume expansion failure
Alternative considered: Allow admins to manually fix PVCs which are stuck in resizing condition
Why it was not used: Relying on manual fixes would block dependent pod restart workflows and risk leaving volumes permanently unusable if expansion repeatedly fails.
Evidence: keps/sig-storage/1790-recover-resize-failure/README.md

Decision [kep-keps-sig-storage-1790-recover-resize-failure]
Context: Recovery from volume expansion failure
Chosen: Recovery from volume expansion failure
Alternative considered: Solving limitation of allowing restore all the way to original size
Why it was not used: It remained an accepted limitation of the proposal, which only allows resizing to amounts strictly higher than the previously registered capacity.
Evidence: keps/sig-storage/1790-recover-resize-failure/README.md

Decision [kep-keps-sig-auth-5681-conditional-authorization]
Context: KEP-5681: Conditional Authorization
Chosen: KEP-5681: Conditional Authorization
Alternative considered: Expose all conditions in AdmissionReview, and have admission plugins “acknowledge” the conditions
Why it was not used: This approach was rejected because exploring it further revealed that it would be overly complex in practice.
Evidence: keps/sig-auth/5681-conditional-authorization/README.md

Decision [kep-keps-sig-auth-5681-conditional-authorization]
Context: KEP-5681: Conditional Authorization
Chosen: KEP-5681: Conditional Authorization
Alternative considered: Propagate an API server-generated request UID to both authorization and admission
Why it was not used: Although this addressed atomicity, it was rejected because it remains an incomplete lasting solution that still depends on users configuring webhooks.
Evidence: keps/sig-auth/5681-conditional-authorization/README.md

Decision [kep-keps-sig-auth-5681-conditional-authorization]
Context: KEP-5681: Conditional Authorization
Chosen: KEP-5681: Conditional Authorization
Alternative considered: Only one ConditionSet exposed as part of SubjectAccessReview status
Why it was not used: Limiting the status to a single condition set prevents users from seeing the complete set of conditional permissions and denials applying to their request.
Evidence: keps/sig-auth/5681-conditional-authorization/README.md

Decision [kep-keps-sig-auth-5681-conditional-authorization]
Context: KEP-5681: Conditional Authorization
Chosen: KEP-5681: Conditional Authorization
Alternative considered: Require the client to annotate its write request with field or label selectors
Why it was not used: This was rejected because it would break client compatibility with redundant request tagging and create ambiguity when evaluating update operations.
Evidence: keps/sig-auth/5681-conditional-authorization/README.md

Decision [kep-keps-sig-auth-5681-conditional-authorization]
Context: KEP-5681: Conditional Authorization
Chosen: KEP-5681: Conditional Authorization
Alternative considered: Extract label and field selectors from the request and current object in etcd, and supply that to the authorization process
Why it was not used: Pre-authorization decoding creates denial-of-service vulnerabilities from oversized payloads and relies on state-dependent authorization, an architectural anti-pattern.
Evidence: keps/sig-auth/5681-conditional-authorization/README.md

Decision [kep-keps-sig-auth-5681-conditional-authorization]
Context: KEP-5681: Conditional Authorization
Chosen: KEP-5681: Conditional Authorization
Alternative considered: Do nothing, force implementers to implement all of this out of tree
Why it was not used: External setups introduce security risks, enforce redundant webhooks per request, lack atomic policy evaluation, and obscure conditional rules from users.
Evidence: keps/sig-auth/5681-conditional-authorization/README.md

Decision [kep-keps-sig-api-machinery-3488-cel-admission-control]
Context: KEP-3488: CEL for Admission Control
Chosen: KEP-3488: CEL for Admission Control
Alternative considered: Duck Typed CRDs
Why it was not used: Coupling configuration and matching rules restricted policy reuse, complicated API server validation, and created severe difficulties for future schema updates.
Evidence: keps/sig-api-machinery/3488-cel-admission-control/README.md

Decision [kep-keps-sig-api-machinery-3488-cel-admission-control]
Context: KEP-3488: CEL for Admission Control
Chosen: KEP-3488: CEL for Admission Control
Alternative considered: OpenAPIv3 `$ref` in CRDs
Why it was not used: CRDs do not currently accommodate these references, necessitating an independent enhancement proposal to add the functionality first.
Evidence: keps/sig-api-machinery/3488-cel-admission-control/README.md

Decision [kep-keps-sig-api-machinery-3488-cel-admission-control]
Context: KEP-3488: CEL for Admission Control
Chosen: KEP-3488: CEL for Admission Control
Alternative considered: `/matchRules` subresource
Why it was not used: Subresources did not fit the desired goal and would introduce substantial engineering and upkeep overhead, particularly regarding CRDs.
Evidence: keps/sig-api-machinery/3488-cel-admission-control/README.md

Decision [kep-keps-sig-api-machinery-3488-cel-admission-control]
Context: KEP-3488: CEL for Admission Control
Chosen: KEP-3488: CEL for Admission Control
Alternative considered: `PolicyConfiguration` kind with config embedded
Why it was not used: Replicating custom resource behaviors, such as automated validation, for embedded configurations is currently impractical within the API server.
Evidence: keps/sig-api-machinery/3488-cel-admission-control/README.md

Decision [kep-keps-sig-api-machinery-3488-cel-admission-control]
Context: KEP-3488: CEL for Admission Control
Chosen: KEP-3488: CEL for Admission Control
Alternative considered: Generate CRDs
Why it was not used: This approach inherited duck-typed CRD weaknesses and caused issues whenever distinct policies needed to share identical configuration data.
Evidence: keps/sig-api-machinery/3488-cel-admission-control/README.md

Decision [kep-keps-sig-api-machinery-3488-cel-admission-control]
Context: KEP-3488: CEL for Admission Control
Chosen: KEP-3488: CEL for Admission Control
Alternative considered: Scopes
Why it was not used: Locating invalid values and reconstructing precise field paths across nested structures was inefficient, overly complex, and prone to traversal errors.
Evidence: keps/sig-api-machinery/3488-cel-admission-control/README.md

Decision [kep-keps-sig-api-machinery-2523-consistent-resource-versions-semantics]
Context: Consistent Resource Version Semantics for List
Chosen: Consistent Resource Version Semantics for List
Alternative considered: Introduce ExactResourceVersion and MinResourceVersion parameters
Why it was not used: It adds conceptual complexity by maintaining three persistent options and forces redundant, less readable query parameters for legacy support.
Evidence: keps/sig-api-machinery/2523-consistent-resource-versions-semantics/README.md

Decision [kep-keps-sig-api-machinery-2523-consistent-resource-versions-semantics]
Context: Consistent Resource Version Semantics for List
Chosen: Consistent Resource Version Semantics for List
Alternative considered: Use syntax in the query string
Why it was not used: This option complicated backward compatibility by requiring redundant parameters and lacked a clean syntax for handling exact matches.
Evidence: keps/sig-api-machinery/2523-consistent-resource-versions-semantics/README.md

Decision [kep-keps-sig-node-5593-configure-the-max-crashloopbackoff-delay]
Context: KEP-5593: Configure the max CrashLoopBackOff delay
Chosen: KEP-5593: Configure the max CrashLoopBackOff delay
Alternative considered: Global override
Why it was not used: Configuring a node-level kubelet setting applies globally rather than offering per-workload customization.
Evidence: keps/sig-node/5593-configure-the-max-crashloopbackoff-delay/README.md

Decision [kep-keps-sig-node-5593-configure-the-max-crashloopbackoff-delay]
Context: KEP-5593: Configure the max CrashLoopBackOff delay
Chosen: KEP-5593: Configure the max CrashLoopBackOff delay
Alternative considered: Per exit code configuration
Why it was not used: The document does not explain why this option was rejected, only noting it was considered to handle specific workload failure categories.
Evidence: keps/sig-node/5593-configure-the-max-crashloopbackoff-delay/README.md

Decision [kep-keps-sig-node-5593-configure-the-max-crashloopbackoff-delay]
Context: KEP-5593: Configure the max CrashLoopBackOff delay
Chosen: KEP-5593: Configure the max CrashLoopBackOff delay
Alternative considered: RestartPolicy: Rapid
Why it was not used: Granting pod authors control over backoff rates risked node stability, while modifying the existing spec enum created complex version skew challenges.
Evidence: keps/sig-node/5593-configure-the-max-crashloopbackoff-delay/README.md

Decision [kep-keps-sig-node-5593-configure-the-max-crashloopbackoff-delay]
Context: KEP-5593: Configure the max CrashLoopBackOff delay
Chosen: KEP-5593: Configure the max CrashLoopBackOff delay
Alternative considered: On Success and the 10 minute recovery threshold
Why it was not used: This option was rejected because it posed overload risks to the node and conflicted with Kubernetes's architectural focus on using pods for persistent rather than exiting workloads.
Evidence: keps/sig-node/5593-configure-the-max-crashloopbackoff-delay/README.md

Decision [kep-keps-sig-node-5593-configure-the-max-crashloopbackoff-delay]
Context: KEP-5593: Configure the max CrashLoopBackOff delay
Chosen: KEP-5593: Configure the max CrashLoopBackOff delay
Alternative considered: Exposing per-node config as command-line flags
Why it was not used: Adding more CLI flags is discouraged, and the KubeletConfiguration API provides a viable per-node alternative now that config directory support reached beta.
Evidence: keps/sig-node/5593-configure-the-max-crashloopbackoff-delay/README.md

Decision [kep-keps-sig-node-5593-configure-the-max-crashloopbackoff-delay]
Context: KEP-5593: Configure the max CrashLoopBackOff delay
Chosen: KEP-5593: Configure the max CrashLoopBackOff delay
Alternative considered: Late recovery
Why it was not used: It was deemed beyond the scope of the current effort and deferred for future evaluation once the proposal achieves beta status.
Evidence: keps/sig-node/5593-configure-the-max-crashloopbackoff-delay/README.md

Decision [kep-keps-sig-node-5593-configure-the-max-crashloopbackoff-delay]
Context: KEP-5593: Configure the max CrashLoopBackOff delay
Chosen: KEP-5593: Configure the max CrashLoopBackOff delay
Alternative considered: More complex heuristics
Why it was not used: This approach was deferred because dynamic heuristics are difficult to understand, costly to test, and have uncertain value, though they may be reconsidered in future milestones.
Evidence: keps/sig-node/5593-configure-the-max-crashloopbackoff-delay/README.md

Decision [kep-keps-sig-api-machinery-2885-server-side-unknown-field-validation]

Context: KEP-2876: CRD Validation Expression Language

Decision [kep-keps-sig-scheduling-5229-asynchronous-api-calls-during-scheduling]
Context: KEP-5229: Asynchronous API calls during scheduling
Chosen: KEP-5229: Asynchronous API calls during scheduling
Alternative considered: 1: Handle API calls in the scheduling queue
Why it was not used: It was rejected because it increased pod queuing delay, caused inconsistent error handling, grew event tracking overhead, and could not handle nominated nodes natively.
Evidence: keps/sig-scheduling/5229-asynchronous-api-calls-during-scheduling/README.md

Decision [kep-keps-sig-scheduling-5229-asynchronous-api-calls-during-scheduling]
Context: KEP-5229: Asynchronous API calls during scheduling
Chosen: KEP-5229: Asynchronous API calls during scheduling
Alternative considered: 2: Handle API calls in the handleSchedulingFailure
Why it was not used: This approach was rejected because it risks race conditions, demands major restructuring that could introduce circular dependencies, and cannot cover nominated node scenarios.
Evidence: keps/sig-scheduling/5229-asynchronous-api-calls-during-scheduling/README.md

Decision [kep-keps-sig-scheduling-5229-asynchronous-api-calls-during-scheduling]
Context: KEP-5229: Asynchronous API calls during scheduling
Chosen: KEP-5229: Asynchronous API calls during scheduling
Alternative considered: 1: Just dispatch goroutines
Why it was not used: This option was rejected because it cannot delay or combine requests, requires extra mechanisms to prevent update race conditions, and impedes nominated node handling.
Evidence: keps/sig-scheduling/5229-asynchronous-api-calls-during-scheduling/README.md

Decision [kep-keps-sig-scheduling-5229-asynchronous-api-calls-during-scheduling]
Context: KEP-5229: Asynchronous API calls during scheduling
Chosen: KEP-5229: Asynchronous API calls during scheduling
Alternative considered: Proposal A: Create a separate component managing API calls
Why it was not used: Introducing an independent component risked leaving the cache out of sync with outgoing requests, feeding obsolete data to the scheduler.
Evidence: keps/sig-scheduling/5229-asynchronous-api-calls-during-scheduling/README.md

Decision [kep-keps-sig-scheduling-5229-asynchronous-api-calls-during-scheduling]
Context: KEP-5229: Asynchronous API calls during scheduling
Chosen: KEP-5229: Asynchronous API calls during scheduling
Alternative considered: Proposal B: Make a scheduler's cache managing API calls
Why it was not used: It would require heavily refactoring the scheduler's fragmented caches to accommodate custom storage mechanisms and non-Pod requests.
Evidence: keps/sig-scheduling/5229-asynchronous-api-calls-during-scheduling/README.md

Decision [kep-keps-sig-node-6122-configurable-scaling-delay-with-pod-resource-exposure]
Context: KEP-6122: Configurable Scaling Delay with Pod Resource Exposure
Chosen: KEP-6122: Configurable Scaling Delay with Pod Resource Exposure
Alternative considered: LIFO (Last-In, First-Out) CPU Release
Why it was not used: It was turned down because preserving originally granted processors is already mandatory, making LIFO an overly complex tracking system with no real payoff.
Evidence: keps/sig-node/6122-configurable-scaling-delay-with-pod-resource-exposure/README.md

Decision [kep-keps-sig-node-6122-configurable-scaling-delay-with-pod-resource-exposure]
Context: KEP-6122: Configurable Scaling Delay with Pod Resource Exposure
Chosen: KEP-6122: Configurable Scaling Delay with Pod Resource Exposure
Alternative considered: CPU Release Based on Real-Time Usage
Why it was not used: It was rejected because volatile CPU metrics break Kubernetes' predictable resource model and risk harming cache-sensitive workload performance.
Evidence: keps/sig-node/6122-configurable-scaling-delay-with-pod-resource-exposure/README.md

Decision [kep-keps-sig-node-6122-configurable-scaling-delay-with-pod-resource-exposure]
Context: KEP-6122: Configurable Scaling Delay with Pod Resource Exposure
Chosen: KEP-6122: Configurable Scaling Delay with Pod Resource Exposure
Alternative considered: Immediate Actuation (No Delay)
Why it was not used: This option was rejected because removing cores instantly gives time-critical applications no opportunity to reassign tasks, risking severe performance hits.
Evidence: keps/sig-node/6122-configurable-scaling-delay-with-pod-resource-exposure/README.md

Decision [kep-keps-sig-node-6122-configurable-scaling-delay-with-pod-resource-exposure]
Context: KEP-6122: Configurable Scaling Delay with Pod Resource Exposure
Chosen: KEP-6122: Configurable Scaling Delay with Pod Resource Exposure
Alternative considered: Handshake-Based Synchronization
Why it was not used: It was rejected because linking kubelet to application state breaches core Kubernetes design principles and allows workloads to stall scaling indefinitely.
Evidence: keps/sig-node/6122-configurable-scaling-delay-with-pod-resource-exposure/README.md

Decision [kep-keps-sig-node-6122-configurable-scaling-delay-with-pod-resource-exposure]
Context: KEP-6122: Configurable Scaling Delay with Pod Resource Exposure
Chosen: KEP-6122: Configurable Scaling Delay with Pod Resource Exposure
Alternative considered: Node Declared Features as Opt-Out Mechanism
Why it was not used: It was rejected because node declared features are temporary tools tied to feature lifecycles, making them unfit as a lasting opt-out solution.
Evidence: keps/sig-node/6122-configurable-scaling-delay-with-pod-resource-exposure/README.md

Decision [kep-keps-sig-node-6122-configurable-scaling-delay-with-pod-resource-exposure]
Context: KEP-6122: Configurable Scaling Delay with Pod Resource Exposure
Chosen: KEP-6122: Configurable Scaling Delay with Pod Resource Exposure
Alternative considered: Pod-Level Grace Period (Opt-In/Opt-Out Mechanism)
Why it was not used: It was postponed to later releases because altering the Pod API requires wider community consensus, whereas the chosen method enables quicker validation without schema updates.
Evidence: keps/sig-node/6122-configurable-scaling-delay-with-pod-resource-exposure/README.md

Decision [kep-keps-sig-node-6122-configurable-scaling-delay-with-pod-resource-exposure]
Context: KEP-6122: Configurable Scaling Delay with Pod Resource Exposure
Chosen: KEP-6122: Configurable Scaling Delay with Pod Resource Exposure
Alternative considered: Hook-Based Synchronization Approach
Why it was not used: This option was postponed for evaluation in later release phases to potentially enable pod-level opt-in functionality.
Evidence: keps/sig-node/6122-configurable-scaling-delay-with-pod-resource-exposure/README.md

Decision [kep-keps-sig-node-6122-configurable-scaling-delay-with-pod-resource-exposure]

Chosen: KEP-6122: Configurable Scaling Delay with Pod Resource Exposure
